title: Ladder Setup and Use for Drywall Work
summary: Drywall crews climb stepladders and extension ladders all day, often with boards, buckets and tools in hand. This talk covers OSHA's ladder use rules for setup, climbing and inspection.
talking_points: When a portable ladder is used to reach an upper landing, the side rails must extend at least 3 feet above the landing. When that extension is not possible because of the ladder length, the ladder must be secured at its top to a rigid support and a grasping device such as a grabrail provided (29 CFR 1926.1053(b)(1)).
Set a non-self-supporting ladder at an angle where the base is approximately one-quarter of the working length away from the top support (1926.1053(b)(5)(i)).
Use ladders only on stable, level surfaces unless secured (1926.1053(b)(6)). Keep the area around the top and bottom clear (1926.1053(b)(9)).
Ladders in doorways, passageways or other places where traffic can bump them must be secured or the area barricaded (1926.1053(b)(8)). Door openings are common on drywall jobs.
Keep ladders free of oil, grease and other slipping hazards (1926.1053(b)(2)). Wipe off joint compound and other wet material before climbing.
Never use the top or top step of a stepladder as a step, and do not climb the rear cross-bracing unless the ladder is designed for it (1926.1053(b)(13)-(14)).
Do not move, shift or extend a ladder while someone is on it, and do not load it beyond its rated capacity (1926.1053(b)(11), (b)(3)).
Inspect ladders for visible defects. Tag or mark a ladder with broken or missing rungs, split rails or corroded parts and pull it from service until repaired (1926.1053(b)(15)-(16)).
site_hazards_to_check: Ladder set in a doorway or hallway with traffic
Wet compound, mud or dust on rungs and feet
Uneven or slippery floor under the ladder feet
Carrying boards or buckets up the ladder
Standing on the top step or reaching far to the side
discussion_questions: How do we carry boards and tools so both hands are free to climb?
Where can we get a tag for a damaged ladder, and who pulls it?
Where on this floor are ladders most likely to get bumped?
